To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the met-enke-phalin-like immunoreactive substance in the rat Merkel cells is not identical with leu-enke-phalin and is not released by the denervation of the Merkel cells.

Merkel cells exhibit immunoreactivity towards methionine-enkepahlin, a neuropeptide that is known to be present in nerves innervating the skin, and that this immunoreaction is not affected by denervation of Merkel cells.
the Merkel cells from rat sinus hair follicles show immunoreactivity for metenkephaline but not for leu-enke-phalin, and that this immunoreactivity is not affected by denervation of the Merkel cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the paraneuroendocrine system.
the investigation of neuropeptides and GEP-hormones in Merkel cells.
the investigation of the neuroendocrine properties of Merkel cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Merkel cells are neuroendocrine cells with a specific neuropeptide (met-enkephalin)-immunoreactivity.
the Merkel cell system is not a part of the endocrine system but is a paraneuronal sensory system with a possible role as a neuroreceptor.
the Merkel cells of the sinus hair follicles are a neuroendocrine cell with the ability to produce met-enkephaline and to store and release it in a regulated manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Merkel cell may represent a neuroendocrine receptor cell, which is capable of producing met-enkephalins.
Merkel cells may be a part of the endogenous pain control system.
the Merkel cells from the sinus hair follicles are a neuroendocrine cell type which synthesizes and stores met-enkephaline, a peptide which is involved in the regulation of pain and nociception.
The main takeaway from our work is that
met-enkephaline is present in the Merkel cell, but not the associated nerve terminals.
the met-enkeplhalin-like immunoreactivity is restricted to Merkel cells, and not to associated nerve fibers.
the Merkel cell, a cell type that has been implicated in touch sensation, has the ability to synthesize and store a neuropeptide.
